sentences.text: This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.142/2024 registered at Police Station - Naigarhi, District Mauganj (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 306, 34 of IPC.

Applicant is in detention since 19.04.2024.
2.

As per the prosecution story, allegation against the applicant is that she along with other co-accused persons have physically and mentally tortured the deceased due to which the deceased committed suicide by consuming poison.
Police registered the case against the present applicant under the aforesaid Sections.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is in jail since 19.04.2024.
Applicant is innocent and falsely implicated in this case.
She is 65 years old lady.
Applicant is the mother-in-law of the deceased.
It is submitted that marriage of Vijay Yadav, who is the son of applicant and deceased was solemnized 10 years ago.
Present applicant is not the main accused.

As per the statements of witnesses, Vijay Yadav had illicit relationship with his sister-in-law (bhabhi) and he Phoolmati Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2514559/
1 had beaten the deceased.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that ingredients of Section 306 of the IPC is not made out against the present applicant.
There is no criminal record of the applicant.
Trial will take considerable time, therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 439 of the Code o f Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that she shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

She shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE shahina Phoolmati Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2514559/
